newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed higher with spot March supported above $300. Traders reported a mostly routine session, with activity mixed on both sides of the market. March and May closed $1.9 higher to end at $301.20 and $300.90 per tonne respectively. In New York raw sugar futures consolidated after the sharp decline last week. March ended up 11 points at 10.62 cents/lb, while May closed 8 points higher at 10.68 cents/lb. Supplies continue to be abundant and there is little concern about deliverable supplies against the March contract.

INDIA - Since August, 1995, the government has allocated an export quota of 1.269 million tonnes, white value, to the Indian Sugar and General Industries Export-Import Corporation (ISIEC). Of this quantity 1.225 million tonnes were for exports to the world market and 44,000 tonnes for export to the preferential markets of the United States and the European Union. Informed sources said the entire quota announced so far has already been sold out. The latest sale was made by ISIEC to Cosmos International for 12,500 tonnes to Russia at $345 per tonne for shipment in February/March 1997.

The State Trading Corporation has managed to get an allocation of 100,000 tonnes of which it has already sold 30,000 tonnes. In spite of India's activities on the export market there are strong indications that there will be a sharp fall in sugar production this year. The total quantity produced up to December 15, 1996, reached 1.711 million tonnes, 30 per cent less than the 2.445 million tonnes produced in the same year- ago period. Offtake until December 15 was 2.999 million tonnes up from 2.808 million tonnes the previous year. Exports reached 144,000 tonnes, slightly more than the 132,000 tonnes shipped the same period in 1995. However, in spite of the sharp fall in sugar production stocks on December 15 were with 6.470 million tonnes still significantly above last year's figure of 5.103 million tonnes.

Whether the sharp fall in production is indicative for the whole of the season remains to be seen. While some observers expect production to pick up others are of the opinion that production will drop by about 2.0 to 2.5 million tonnes. The shortfall is ascribed to poor crops in Maharashtra (down by almost a million tonnes); Tamil Nadu (down by 500,000 to 600,000 tonnes); Andhra Pradesh (due to a cyclone) and also the late crushing; in Uttar Pradesh due to legal battles between millers, state government and growers.

BRAZIL - Brazil's center south sugar harvest reached 10.22 million tonnes, tel quel, in 1996/97 (May/December), up 9.1 percent from the 9.37 million tonnes produced in 1995/96, Consultants Datanet Agricommodities said. Sugar cane output totalled 227.49 million tonnes, rise of 11.3 percent on the 204.40 million tonnes harvested in 1995/96 and a new record. According to data net Sao Paulo state showed a 10 per cent increase in sugar cane production in 1996/97 while other states in the center south region - Parana, Minas Gerais, Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul and Goias - saw a 17 per cent rise.

AUSTRALIA - Sugar exports in November 1996 reached 382,432 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 440,330 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in the first half of 1996/97 (June/November) up to 3.101 million tonnes, up on last year's 3.0 million tonnes. Major countries of destination in June/November 1996 were Canada with 584,482 tonnes raws against 422,706 tonnes, Malaysia with 458,958 tonnes compared to 440,521 tonnes, South Korea with 449,075 tonnes against 409,143 tonnes and Japan with 445,308 tonnes, down from 570,133 tonnes. Also in November the first shipment of raw sugar to Saudi Arabia left Australia. In Saudi Arabia a new refinery started trial runs in December 1996. White sugar exports from Australia seem to have stabilized. Shipments in June/November 1996 amounted to 121,654 tonnes, down from last year's 127,308 tonnes. Major countries of destination in 1996 were New Zealand with 33,187 tonnes against nil and Indonesia with 20,671 tonnes compared to 19,461 tonnes.

The European Union awarded 47,250 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 46.302 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on Wednesday. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to January 15 reached 1,345,750 tonnes, which compares to 1,508,175 tonnes last year. Iran bought a cargo of white sugar for delivery in Feb/Mar at $306 per tonne. Further details were not immediately available. Syria will hold a buying tender for two cargoes of either white or raw sugar for delivery in February/March. Syria tendered on December 14 to buy 13,000 tonnes of white sugar and 13,000 tonnes of raws but cancelled it due to a mistake in the terms submitted by one potential supplier.
